status: development review; detailed API contract not implemented
status_basis: Conversation decisions; source comparison; historical model-extraction evidence; package-layout numeric/AST checks, wheel import verification, and full suite rerun in both staging and the applied worktree. Revision 03 reorganizes the document only; it does not rerun or supersede the recorded numerical checks. Revision 04 separates document scope from tool development goals and initial support scope; it changes documentation only. Revision 05 extends the system workflow through results, observables, visualization and storage, and describes block responsibilities. The diagram is a target architecture; existing implementation foundations and future extensions are distinguished. No code or detailed API contract changes. Revision 06 splits the workflow diagram into input preparation and calculation/result use, followed by the existing responsibility table. It changes slide layout and explanatory wording only. Revision 07 aligns the geometry block directly below system construction and clarifies the classical spin configuration as a separate initial configuration for optimization or reference configuration for LSWT. No API or implementation changes. Revision 08 clarifies the computational spin system as the model instantiated with calculation geometry and names the classical state inputs as spin directions and magnetic-structure periodicity. Documentation terminology only. Revision 09 records the 1st development scope and contract decisions made with the user on 2026-09-29: model as Hamiltonian, external-variable classes, state-geometry commensurability, terms[] schema with bilinear and zeeman kinds, g-tensor with external B and -mu_B sign, square/triangular Heisenberg benchmarks with a minimal ED verification tool, spintoolkit package target, and Kitaev as a later benchmark. The detailed contract Markdown was updated first; details not decided by the user are marked as proposals. No code or numerical evidence changes. Revision 10 records the user's decisions on the four detail proposals: optional zeeman terms with a warning when B is nonzero and a site has none, the g_(alpha beta) index convention, mu_B = 1 for relative energy units, and a split between state validation and reference-state diagnostics (stationarity, Colpa stability). No code or numerical evidence changes. Revision 11 records the user's decisions on open items: the standard Fourier sign with the full-position gauge as a toolkit convention (theory canon status unchanged), the resulting NBCP displacement reading r_target = r_source - d with a conversion rule to be confirmed numerically in stage 2 by elementwise H(k) comparison, the split of state/request/result into common and method-specific parts with SpinState, common request, result header and LSWT body drafts, and spintoolkit/models/ for standard benchmarks. The displacement coverage check was rerun on the current code; no code or numerical evidence changes. Revision 12 is a cleanup: the contract was split into the transfer contract and the 1st development plan (content preserved, decisions tagged D01-D15), the decided detail-rules page moved to appendix B, the two displacement pages were merged, and an unused macro was removed. No content, code or numerical evidence changes. Revision 13 records stage 0: the package rename lswt -> spintoolkit (methods/spin_wave -> methods/lswt) with a code-space/lswt compatibility package, verified against baseline commit 49f047a by per-test-ID pytest comparison, a 208-value numerical snapshot (maximum difference 0), compatibility tests, an offline wheel build and an editable reinstall. Source paths in this manifest now point to code-space/spintoolkit. Revision 14 records stage 1: SpinModel, SpinState, ExternalConditions, CalculationGeometry with validation, a classical energy/field/torque consumer and the Heisenberg benchmarks (D16), verified by exact classical energies, finite-difference fields, an NBCP cross-check against the existing EnergyFunction, 53 new tests, unchanged outcomes for the 225 existing tests and the 208-value snapshot. Revision 15 records the fix of the quantum path of SpinOptimizer.find_minimum (commit d43d8d4: DE fallback with E_cl + E_qm comparison, no in-place mutation of the DE angles; 225 passed / same 5 failed, 208-value snapshot difference 0), a concise description of the current classical/MAGSWT/quantum search paths, and the user's decision D17: zero-point state selection only on the classical ground-state manifold, along the orbit R_n(phi) whose axis is fixed by the classical Hessian null space, with an E_cl constancy check. The axis rule was checked numerically on the NBCP Y state (examples/nbcp_y_orbit_axis_check.py). The contract Markdown was updated first. D17 is not implemented. Merged after stage 1 (revision 14), so the state-selection decision is numbered D17; after the merge 278 passed / same 5 failed and the 208-value snapshot difference is 0. Revision 16 records the angle_setting=None fix (commit 8f4dd1e; 280 passed / same 5 failed, snapshot difference 0), numbers for the open D17 criteria from examples/nbcp_y_orbit_criteria_check.py (null-space rules on 18 DE runs: fixed tolerance 8/12, gap ratio 12/12, polish then fixed tolerance 12/12, no false positives; sixfold E_qm amplitude within 1.1% of the converged lambda_6 at N=6 and minimum at phi = 0 mod pi/3 for all N >= 3) with review proposals that are not decisions, and a correction: the J_Gamma = 0.010 spread is a converged selection, not an unreliable one. Revision 17 records D18 (D17 implementation plan: remove the unconstrained E_cl+E_qm 'quantum' path with the D17 implementation and warn until then, keep MAGSWT pending a reproduction check, place D17 as stage 2b, limit the triangular benchmark to h = 0 and h > h_sat) and D19 (selectable physical or fixed-constant criteria with defaults in definitions/defaults.py). Revision 18 records D20: dimensionless numerics in the coefficient energy unit E0 (field = mu_B B / E0, temperature = k_B T / E0), Units and unit conversion removed; physical units T, K, meV are a documented convention converted by the user. Revision 19 records stage 2 (D21): NBCP common model with published parameter sets and candidate states, SpinSystem conversion in both directions, and D13 confirmed by element-wise H(k) agreement (1.7e-16) with the legacy builders. Revision 20 records stage 2b (D22): zero-point state selection on the classical manifold (methods/state_selection.select_on_manifold) with an analytic tangent-space Hessian and classical refinement (methods/classical), the D19 physics-mode coefficients chosen at implementation (for user review), and removal of the unconstrained 'quantum' optimizer. NBCP Y (0.2 T) and V (1.4 T) with J_PD or J_Gamma = 0.010 meV are selected in both modes at N = 6 and 12 with harmonic amplitudes and curvatures within 1.1% (N = 6) and 0.2% (N = 12) of independent N = 48 scans; the 1.64e-12 J_Gamma Y-state splitting is resolved about 900 times above the fit threshold. DE starts, controls, triangular 120-degree and square polarized benchmarks and the MAGSWT reproduction are recorded; 373 passed / same 5 failed, 208-value snapshot difference 0. Revision 21 records stage 3 (D23): finite-torus expansion with rules shared by all methods (duplicated bonds summed, bonds folding onto one site rejected in classical, ED and LSWT comparisons), a general exact-diagonalization tool with optional U(1) magnetization and translation-momentum sectors, one-magnon ED equal to the LSWT bands at every torus momentum within 1.6e-14 in nine cases including DM (the -k pairing fails, fixing the momentum sign), symmetry-free spectra equal to an independent Kronecker construction within 4.6e-14, and the 4x4 square S = 1/2 ground state -0.7017802 per site; 404 passed / same 5 failed, 208-value snapshot difference 0. Revision 22 records stage 4a (D24): solve_lswt on the common model types with the common result header and JSON output, default regularization 'none' with zero modes reported (an exact Goldstone mode made positive by round-off is caught by a relative tolerance), diagonalization data kept for reuse, exact reproduction of LSWTSolver on NBCP, convergence to the analytic square and triangular LSWT values, and approximate comparisons with QMC and DMRG; 421 passed / same 5 failed, 208-value snapshot difference 0. Revision 23 records stage 4b (D25): zero-mode scan in three classes from lambda_min(H)/scale with a user decision step for candidates, Goldstone/accidental/line zero modes distinguished, dimensionless finite-temperature F, U, S, C and moments reusing the stored diagonalization, and agreement with ED below exp(-2 Delta/t) at low temperature; 437 passed / same 5 failed, 208-value snapshot difference 0. Revision 24 records stage 4c (D26): mode-resolved one-magnon structure factor and exact Bragg intensities equal to ED matrix elements within 1e-15, Neel analytic weights, sum rules on the extended mesh, bond correlations reproducing E_GS, and the diagnosis of the existing correlations module (per-cell normalization and a doubled sublattice phase); 452 passed / same 5 failed, 208-value snapshot difference 0. Revision 25 records the cleanup of existing code (D27): the MAGSWT grid search and the unverified observables/correlations.py are removed; orbit_energy_landscape, spin_correlation and to_ladder replace them; the NBCP examples use the classical search followed by select_on_manifold; 457 passed / same 5 failed, the 144 remaining snapshot values unchanged (64 leaves of the removed MAGSWT searches reported as not compared). Revision 26 adds the review proposal D28 (not a decision): the classical-quantum comparison by the one-loop effective potential on the relaxed soft path, with its check (D17 limit reproduced, the rigid orbit overestimates classical pinning by a factor 14 for Y at 1.7 degrees, correcting the provisional statement). No code change.
document_purpose: Development document for implementing a 2D spin-system solver: physical information representation, required functionality and implementation methods. Document scope is distinguished from tool development goals and initial support scope; implementation and verification evidence stays in appendices.
